annotations.title: CPC Order 39 Rule 1: Cases in which temporary injunction may be granted | IndiaCode

content.text:
Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, allows courts to grant temporary injunctions in certain situations:

- If property in dispute is at risk of being wasted, damaged, or alienated by any party, or wrongfully sold in execution of a decree.

- If the defendant threatens or intends to remove or dispose of property to defraud creditors.

- If the defendant threatens to dispossess the plaintiff or cause injury related to any property in dispute.

In such cases, the court may issue a temporary injunction to restrain these actions or make other orders to prevent harm until the suit is resolved or further orders are given. ([indiacode.ecourtsindia.com](https://indiacode.ecourtsindia.com/cpc/order/xxxix/rule/1/?utm_source=openai))
